A few things worth asking.

Practical answers before you invite your team.

Do I need mobile data to score a game?

Not all the time. In a supported Coach app, or the Parent app when you are the assigned scorer, open and refresh the fixture online on match day before kick-off. If signal drops, match actions can save on your phone. Reopen the app with an internet connection as soon as possible after the game, within 24 hours, to send the saved updates. Stay signed in until everything has synced. Other people see updates once they have synced. Scoring in a web browser needs a connection.

Does the app need to stay open for the whole match?

No. You can lock the screen between actions; the match clock works out the time when you return. Wait for each action to show it has saved before leaving. Reopen the app to record the next event, and keep it open with a connection afterwards until all updates have synced. You can leave Keep screen awake switched off.

Will scoring use a lot of battery?

Battery use varies by phone, battery condition, screen brightness and signal. We are still measuring real match-day use, so we cannot promise a typical percentage yet. Leaving Keep screen awake off lets you lock the screen between actions.

How will this actually help me?

You can check availability, share the venue and arrival time, choose a squad and keep parents updated from the same team workspace. Player details and development records stay there for the next session.

What is the difference between Match Day, Team and Club?

Match Day helps you prepare the squad, record the game and send live alerts to families. Team brings your calendar, availability, communication and player development together. Club connects multiple teams in one shared organisation.

Do parents use the same app as Coaches?

Parents have their own view of invitations, shared fixtures, messages and match updates. They connect to their player, while Coaches manage the team.

Can a parent record the match?

Yes. A Coach can assign an authorised parent scorer. The scorer records the events and sends the finished match to the Coach to review and conclude.

Can I use my existing account?

Yes. Choose your Coach or Parent sign-in to open your Football Player workspace.

How much does it cost?

Football Player offers a free Matchday account and paid Team and Club plans. Create your account to choose a plan, or talk to us about the right setup for your club.

Let’s get your team set up.

One squad or a whole club, tell us what you need. We’ll help you find the right place to start.

Player development

See the player.
Build their
next step.

The good first touch. The better decision. The confidence to try again. Keep those observations, give them context and turn them into feedback a player can use.

Football Player brings assessments, coaching notes and development history together on the web and in your apps.

Explore the toolsSee the web and apps

A useful review.
A clear next step.

Capture what happened while you remember it. Return to it when you need it. Give the next assessment something to build on.

Assess the player

Record scores and observations for squad or trial players. Choose the relevant development fields and add the context behind your judgement.

Keep the history

Look back at saved records, dates and Coach comments. Use previous assessments as a reference when writing the next one.

Share useful feedback

Keep a record internal or prepare a parent update. Review the content and choose what belongs in the report before sharing it.

Your players.
Your assessment.

Go beyond broad ratings. Assess the skills, decisions and habits that matter to your team, and add custom fields for the detail you want to track.

Relevant to their age.
Right for their level.

A player finding their feet and an experienced player need different feedback. Your Coaches set the expectations, choose the fields and explain what progress looks like.

Explore an example below to see how the focus can change.

U11 to U14 · Developing

Example assessment focus

Link technique to decisions: look up before receiving, choose a pass and move to support the next action.

For younger players, start with encouragement.

Focus on enjoyment, confidence, trying new skills and individual progress. Record what went well, something the player is beginning to do, and one simple idea to explore next.

For this age group, our example uses coaching observations rather than numerical ratings.

This separate example is for a structured academy programme with Coach-defined assessment criteria. Selecting Experienced alone does not enable ratings for this age group. This is not an FA rule or an elite-player exemption.

First touchPassing choicesReceiving under pressureSupport playDefensive positioningResponse to feedback

What went well

Joined in enthusiastically and tried using both feet with the ball.

What they’re exploring

Starting to look up and notice a teammate before passing.

Next small step

Try finding a little space to receive the ball in the next game.

What the Coach might look for

Can the player repeat the action in a small-sided game, with occasional prompts and some pressure?

Track what matters
to your team.

First touch, weaker-foot passing, finishing, scanning, movement off the ball, tackling, 1v1 defending, goalkeeping, communication, confidence, decision-making and more.

These are examples you can build into your form. Keep broad ratings where they help, or add specific fields to reflect your coaching priorities.

  • Name your own fields and choose the response type
  • Set required fields and organise their order
  • Include selected custom scores in progression charts

Try adding your own development field

    Your player development form

    Edit fields

    Build a form, complete it and download your PDF. Your entries stay in this tab and are cleared when you refresh or leave the page. They are not saved to an account or sent to anyone. Age and level examples illustrate a coaching approach, not an automatic rating or a prescribed development standard.

    More than
    a number.

    A rating needs context. Set expectations for the player’s age group, experience and playing level, then use your notes to explain the judgement. A 7 for one group is not a like-for-like comparison with a 7 for another.

    5 / 10
    Expected Level

    The player is broadly meeting the expected level for their age/team.

    Strengths

    Make the positive feedback specific. Record what the player can repeat, build on and take confidence from.

    Improvements

    Explain the next focus in practical terms. “Check your shoulder before receiving” gives the player something to practise.

    Overall comments

    Bring the assessment together. Add the wider context that separate ratings cannot capture on their own.

    The fields you need

    Add custom fields in the form builder: scores from 1 to 10, numbers, short text, longer notes and choice lists. Choose required fields, organise their order and decide which custom scores appear in progression charts.

    Room to review.
    Ready when you need it.

    Use the web portal for a fuller view of the record. Use the apps to return to player information and follow the feedback shared with your family.

    In the web portal

    Previous development records sit alongside the assessment workflow, so you can read earlier scores and comments before recording a fresh observation.

    Prepare the assessment

    Choose the player, keep the team and session context together, and complete the relevant fields.

    Refer back with care

    Earlier records are there for reference. Their notes are not automatically added to the new assessment.

    Follow progression

    Review saved assessments and score trends from the player profile. Dated scored records give the chart its history.

    With the Coach.

    Open the player profile to find development alongside contacts, private notes and match stats. The latest record and score give you a starting point, with recent records available to open.

    • Find the player’s saved development history
    • Revisit earlier feedback before your next review
    • Keep private Coach notes separate from shared reports

    With the family.

    The Parent app gives families a place to find shared development reports for their linked player. It keeps the coaching feedback in the same app as their fixtures, invitations and match updates.

    • Find Development under More
    • Follow reports shared for the active player
    • Switch between linked players and teams

    From observation
    to the next session.

    A repeatable way to keep feedback useful, whether you are reviewing a trial player or a familiar member of the squad.

    1. 01

      Choose the player

      Start with the correct team and player. Add the relevant session context so the record makes sense when you return to it.

    2. 02

      Look back, then assess

      Read earlier records where available. Record what you see now, using the relevant scores, strengths, improvements and comments.

    3. 03

      Decide what to share

      Keep the record internal or prepare an update for selected parent contacts. Review the report fields and the email or PDF output before sending.

    4. 04

      Return to the next step

      Use the saved history at the next review. Compare your observations and score trends, then agree what the player should keep working on.

    Development, explained.

    How the records, scores and shared feedback fit together.

    Can I assess trial players as well as squad players?

    Yes. The assessment workflow supports trial and squad players. Keep each record attached to the correct player and team.

    Can we add our own assessment fields?

    Yes. Authorised users with custom-field access can create score, number, text, longer-note and choice fields. Fields can be enabled, ordered and marked as required. Custom score fields can also be included in progression charts.

    How should age group and player level affect an assessment?

    Set expectations for the players you coach, taking their age group, experience and playing level into account. Choose suitable fields and describe what you expect to see. The examples above demonstrate that approach; they are not automatic age-based ratings.

    Do I have to score every area?

    Use the relevant enabled fields for your assessment. The written observations explain the score and help the player understand the next step.

    How does the younger-player example work?

    Selecting U7 to U10 defaults to written observations and encouragement. The numeric score guide is hidden and custom fields start with Short text. A separate Structured academy assessment example can be selected explicitly; choosing Experienced alone does not switch ratings on. These are website examples, not an FA age restriction or a change to your app settings.

    How are the standard scores described?

    The standard guide runs from 1 to 10. A score of 5 means Expected Level for the player’s age/team context. Use the guide above to explore the descriptions.

    Does the previous assessment get copied into the new one?

    No. Previous development records are shown for reference. Their notes are not automatically added to the new record.

    Can I see progress over time?

    The player profile brings together saved records and progression charts. A trend needs at least two suitable dated scored records for the selected line. Read the notes alongside the numbers for context.

    Does saving a record automatically send it to parents?

    No. The assessment workflow includes an internal-only option. You choose whether to prepare a parent update and which contacts and report fields to include.

    Can I create an email or PDF report?

    Yes. The web assessment workflow includes email and PDF output options. Review the selected content and recipients before sharing.

    Where do families find shared development reports?

    In the Parent app, open More, then Development. The active player determines which linked player’s information you are viewing.

    Which option includes player development?

    Team and Club include player development tools for assessments, progress tracking and shared feedback. Explore Teams for one squad, or explore Clubs to support Coaches across your organisation.

    Give the next review
    something to build on.

    Tell us how you assess your players today. We’ll show you how the web portal, Coach app and Parent app fit your development process.

Give your Coaches a place to run their teams and your families a club they recognise. Football Player connects the day-to-day work across multiple squads.

A familiar club identity

Use your badge, club name and public contact details across the relevant Coach and parent views.

A team space for Coaches

A shared place to work

Club tools and individual team workspaces sit within the same Football Player platform.

Support the club.
Keep teams moving.

Club admins manage the shared setup. Coaches manage the week. Parents follow the information connected to their player.

A shared home for your teams.

Club tools and team access keep the organisation connected while each squad gets on with its football.

Start with the people
who will use it.

A club system only helps when the Coach on a wet Tuesday and the parent checking the next fixture can use it too.

01

Set the club up

Add your recognised badge, name and contact details. Give the club a consistent starting point.

02

Bring in the teams

Connect Coaches with their squads and get the right people into the right team workspace.

03

Bring in the parents

Link parents to their player so invitations, shared plans and match updates reach the people who need them.

Your club identity

Your kit.
Your colours. Your club.

Show the detail that makes your team recognisable, from stripes and patterns to your badge and sponsor.

These Cambourne home and away kit examples show how a club’s own shirt artwork can go beyond a generic solid-colour kit.

Ready for Match Day

Home or away.
The right kit on show.

Your Club Admin uploads and updates Home and Away kit pictures in Club Profile. When scheduling a match, coaches choose Home kit, Away kit or TBC so families can see which kit to wear.

When your kits change, update the pictures once in Club Profile and the change appears across the club.

Hover over or tap a kit to enlarge it. Illustrative examples with fictional player and fixture details.

Questions from clubs.

A shared system should make the individual team’s job easier.

Can each team keep its own squad and fixtures?

Yes. Teams have their own day-to-day workspaces and records within the club structure.

Who controls the badge and club details?

Authorised club admins manage the shared club identity and contact details.

Do Coaches automatically see every team?

No. Access follows the teams and roles they are authorised to manage.

Can parents switch between linked players?

Yes. The Parent app includes an active-player selector for the player and team context they want to follow.

Where can we explore the tools for our Coaches?

Visit Teams for the weekly workflow and Development for assessments, player history and shared feedback.

your whole club.

About us

For the love of
grassroots football.

Built by a parent, coach, team admin and fan. For every player pulling on their boots, and everyone who helps them get there.

Our story
Why Football Player was built

We’re part of
your touchline.

Football Player grew out of life around grassroots football: organising the team, coaching the players, being a parent and loving the game.

We saw good availability tools with useful features. Some served lots of sports. Meanwhile, team conversations could still end up scattered across messaging apps, with important details getting lost along the way.

When we looked at player development tools, we struggled to find the right fit for younger players, communication with families and grassroots budgets.

So we set out to bring those things together in a platform built around football and the people who make it happen.

What makes us different

The whole player.
The whole football week.

Our starting point is the grassroots game, from the next training session to the excitement of match day.

01

Football comes first

Fixtures, squads, availability and match updates belong together. Football Player brings the organisation around the game into one football-focused place.

02

Development includes families

A player’s progress is more than the final score. Shared development reports help coaches and parents keep the conversation going, with private coaching notes kept separate.

03

Grassroots is our starting point

Volunteer time, younger players and team budgets shaped why we built Football Player. We believe every player and every team should have the opportunity to be the best they want to be.

What we believe

Every player who puts on their boots should feel like a superstar.

Whatever their level. Whatever their ambition. The effort, the progress and the joy of being part of a team all deserve to be celebrated.

Bring the family into the moment

They can’t always
be there.
They still care.

Parents love watching their superstars. They love hearing about the matches, the goals and the moments that made their player smile.

Work, distance and everyday life mean the people who care can’t make every game. We want them to feel part of the excitement, wherever they are.

Match updates help connected parents and invited family fans follow along. Access stays linked to the player and their authorised connections.

Explore Match Day
Who it’s for

Everyone around the game.

Players

At the heart of it all. Their progress, their confidence and their enjoyment of football.

Coaches & team admins

The people planning sessions, organising squads and helping every player find their feet.

Clubs

The people supporting teams and creating a place where grassroots football can thrive.

Parents & family fans

The lifts, the encouragement and the support, on the touchline or following through an invitation.

At Football Player, we want every player, team, coach, parent and fan to feel the match-day excitement.
